description: Separate DATA from CHROME. Extract the actual report data out of the supplied HTML/PDF test files into structured, well-documented Python dataclasses/dicts that can be serialised to JSON, one schema per report type. Static chrome (fixed headings, TOTAL row labels, ministry banner text, column headers) is NOT data and stays in the templates; everything else (region='Mwanza', council='Mwanza CC', exam name, school lists, student rows with name/sex/results/ranking, school & subject performance figures, GPA, competency, ranks) is data. Depends on FEAT-002 so the recovered model already carries correct colours. This feature builds ON TOP of the existing extract.py Document model rather than replacing it.
steps: Inventory the report types by studying the 19 documents (use `sars list` and the compare images). Group them by hierarchy level (council / region / school) and by purpose/variant (overall vs private vs government schools rank; top-10 schools; top-10/best students overall and subjectwise; schools rank subjectwise; subjects rank; wards rank; district performance; mock mobility; EDK/English single-subject rank; single-school result slip). Document the grouping in a REPORT_TYPES catalogue (e.g. src/sars/reports.py) mapping each source document name to a report_type id + level + variant.

Design one dataclass schema per report type in a new module (e.g. src/sars/schema.py). Each schema captures ONLY the data, with clear field names and docstrings describing what each field means. Examples: a SchoolResultSlip has school metadata (centre no, name, region, council, ward) and students [{cno, name, sex, subject_results:{subject:grade}, aggregate, division, points, ranking}] plus school & subject performance summaries; a SchoolsRankReport has region, council, exam_name, rows [{sno, school_name, registered:{f,m,t}, sat:{f,m,t}, division_perf:{...}, gpa, competency, rank}] and a TOTAL/summary row's DATA (the numbers, not the label); a BestStudentsReport has student rows; a SubjectsRankReport has subject rows. Keep exam_name, region, council, ward etc. as data fields (region defaults conceptually to 'Mwanza', council to 'Mwanza CC', but store whatever is extracted).

Write an extractor layer (e.g. src/sars/extract_data.py) that converts a recovered Document (from extract_document + classify) into the appropriate schema instance: walk the classified tables, use classify.py's row_kinds to skip header/banner/total CHROME rows and read the DATA rows into the schema, mapping columns to fields using the header labels. Reuse HEADER_TERMS to locate columns. The competency colour is derived deterministically via the FEAT-002 competency module from the competency/GPA value, so it need not be stored as a colour in the data (store the competency LABEL and GPA; colour is computed at render time).

Add JSON serialisation: each schema is dataclass-based so `dataclasses.asdict` + `json.dumps` works; provide `to_json()`/`from_json()` (or module-level helpers) and confirm round-trip. Optionally add a CLI subcommand `sars data --only "<name>"` that prints/writes the extracted JSON to output/data/<name>.json so the extracted data can be inspected and stored.
Write a JSON data file per document into output/data/ (or a committed sample subset) so the extracted, structured data is visible and reusable, demonstrating 'extract them and store' per the request.
Record in findings: the report_type catalogue, the list of schemas with their field shapes, the mapping from document -> schema, and the location of the emitted JSON.
acceptance_criteria: A schema module defines a documented dataclass per report type; each field's meaning is clear from its name/docstring and only DATA (no fixed headings/labels) is stored.
A reports catalogue maps every one of the 19 documents to a report_type id + level (council/region/school) + variant (overall/private/government/subjectwise/etc.).

An extractor turns a classified Document into the correct schema instance, correctly reading student rows (name, sex, results, ranking) and school/subject performance figures, and skipping chrome rows.
Each schema round-trips through JSON (asdict -> json.dumps -> load -> reconstruct) without loss.
Extracted JSON data files are produced (e.g. output/data/*.json) for the documents.
verification: . .venv/bin/activate && python -c "from sars import reports, schema; print(len(reports.CATALOGUE))"
